_meta.description: Randomised global-shop bundle products: what each paid out, banded by the buyer's level.
_meta.authoritative: every reward appeared verbatim in a retail purchase response; nothing is interpolated
_meta.why: these four products are ABSENT from the APK offer catalogue, so the server had no authored contents and replayed one captured reward per product -- every purchase byte-identical, which is #170. Retail re-rolled every time: 4,697 purchases of the biggest bundle produced 4,697 distinct rewards.
_meta.levelKeying: MEASURED, not assumed. The payout scales with the buyer's level (median 16,985 gold at level 5-9, 46,659 at 23-28, 60,687 at 62). Pooling would hand a low level player a high level payout.
_meta.levelAttribution: the purchase response carries no level (30 of 6,310), so each purchase is attributed to the character in its URL and that character's level at the NEAREST /characters observation in capture order. Players level up during the corpus, so one level per character would be wrong. Purchases with no attributable level are counted in droppedForNoLevel and DROPPED.
_meta.howToDraw: pick the product, then the band containing the buyer's level (nearest band if none contains it), then draw one whole reward weighted by n. Mint a fresh uuid4 for every granted item.
_meta.instanceIdsStripped: items[].id removed; the consumer MUST mint one per purchase. properties.GRADING/ENCHANTING[].id are shared property DEFINITION ids and are KEPT -- stripping them makes the corpus undeserializable.
_meta.sampling: every observed reward is distinct, so a band is a sample bank rather than a weighted distribution. Bands larger than maxSamplesPerBand are thinned systematically (every k-th in capture order), which preserves the spread over time; observations records the true count before thinning.
